we have fabricated hybrid Si nanostructures integrated with plasmonic nanostructures using top-down lithography and have demonstrated that the PL of Si NDs are greatly enhanced by the plasmonic nanostructure, depending on their size and shape.

the authors study plasmonics enhancements of photoluminiscence in hybrid Si nanodisk arrays with Au nanostructures, where these hybrid structures are fabricated using fully top-down lithgraphy: neutral-beam-etching using bio-nano-template and high-resolution electron beam lithography.
plasmonic enhancements are observed in Si NDs by hybridizing with Au nanostructures and that the enhancements depend on the shape, size, and separation distance of the Au nanostructures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
plasmonic effects in hybrid Si nanostructure arrays with nanostructured Au.
the fabrication of hybrid Si-Au nanocomposites and their plasmonic enhancements on photoluminescence.
the fabrication of hybrid nanostructures with precise control over the separation distance between the two components and with plasmonic enhancements in the hybrid Si nanostructures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the authors have demonstrated a new approach to fabricate hybrid nanostructures by combining top-down and bottom-up lithography techniques and have observed plasmonic enhancements in Si NDs integrated with Au nanoplates.
this paper presents a novel method to enhance the PL in Si nanostructures by integrating with plasmonic nanostructures.
the authors have shown that the hybridization of Au nanoplates with Si ND arrays enhances PL in the Si ND arrays.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the PL enhancement is attributed to the localized surface plasmon (LSP) resonances in the Au nanoplates, where the PL enhancement is more pronounced when the Si NDs and the Au nanoplates are in close contact with each other.
the PL intensity in the Si ND can be enhanced by the plasmonic coupling with Au nanostructures fabricated by fully topdown lithography.
plasmonic effects can be used as a tool for controlling the optical properties of Si nanostructures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hybrid nanostructures with a precise control of the separation distance can be used to design and optimize the plasmonic enhancements for various optical devices.
fully top-down fabrication of hybrid nanostructures with precise control of separation distance can be an important step toward the realization of highly integrated photonic devices.
the PL enhancement in the Si ND array is achieved by integrating with the hybrid nanostructures of Au nanoplates fabricated by fully topdown lithography.
